evidence.reproduction: Run `sed -n '1,240p' src/notes.mjs` from /workspace and inspect the complete function.
evidence.observedBehavior: The module declares `export function summarizeNotes(records)`. It filters with `!record.archived`, maps each active record to a fresh `{ id: record.id, title: record.title.trim() }` object, sorts the derived array with direct string `<` and `>` comparison by title and then id, and synchronously returns `{ activeCount: notes.length, archivedCount: records.length - notes.length, notes }`. Sorting occurs after map on the derived array, not on records. With the documented boolean archived flags, the two count expressions count false and true flags respectively. The same direct pipeline yields zero counts and an empty notes array for empty input.

The command exited 0 with 1 test file passing, 0 failures, and 0 skipped tests.

evidence.reproduction: Run `node --input-type=module` from /workspace, import summarizeNotes, and call it with `[{id:'b',title:' x ',archived:false},{id:'a',title:'x',archived:false},{id:'D',title:'apple',archived:false},{id:'C',title:'Apple',archived:false},{id:'e',title:' archived ',archived:true}]`; snapshot the result, compare serialized input before and after, check returned/input identities, verify the result is not a Promise, mutate result.notes[0].title, and observe records[3].title.
evidence.observedBehavior: Before result mutation, the output was `{activeCount:4,archivedCount:1,notes:[{id:'C',title:'Apple'},{id:'D',title:'apple'},{id:'a',title:'x'},{id:'b',title:'x'}]}`. The archived record was absent, uppercase `Apple` preceded lowercase `apple`, and equal `x` titles were ordered by IDs `a` then `b`. The serialized input remained unchanged, every returned note had a new identity, editing the first returned title left its input title as `Apple`, and the result was not a Promise.
